items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: he was a pianist and he told me, he says, study, he was a dogmatic man. Don't come to my house unless you have some music and don't make no bad notes in here

ctx.x: So, all right, everybody come back and by that time Mama was telling me something else, and I'm looking around talking halfway bassing, see, I done grow too big for Mama so when Mama really wants something happen, Mama would grab me by the arm and drop that tooth on me and bite me so badly, yes, Mama, anything, she'd be chewing on me. Mama was a very small woman, she had very small feet and small -- and whatever Mama wanted done, I did that, and did it quickly, and nothing was no problem.

So it seems like, I was going to school and everything and then I think I was about 13 -- I had a little ukele and was playing it (unintelligible) and there was a man named Emmy Lucas, he worked down through Harditch's Brewery and they sent him to school and he was a genius. He knew all the music, that's what he did and he was a pianist and he told me, he says, study, he was a dogmatic man. Don't come to my house unless you have some music and don't make no bad notes in here, go home, these kind of things, so I…

I was working to get a clarinet and my mother sent me to Louisiana on vacation and I had an accident which changed everything, because I used to be a good swimmer and good runner and I boxed and everything and was doing pretty good, but by the way, when I was about two years, or three years old, I saw my mother and the streetcar was coming up the street and I ran to meet my mother and the streetcar cut the sandal off from my ankle, so, I'll tell you about that later.
